    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Adexchanger ↗ Open Full Page

    Going Straight To The C-Suite; All I Want For Christmas Is Hess Truck Ads In September

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (865 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Pinch your nose and blow gently through your nostrils.
    • That’s how to unpop your eardrums on a plane, or after taking the elevator from the lowly marketer offices to the executive floor.
    • It has been revealed that earlier this month, this newsletter noted the trend of holdco CEOs making handshake deals with brand CEOs to poach accounts their agencies didn’t even pitch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pinch your nose and blow gently through your nostrils.

    That’s how to unpop your eardrums on a plane, or after taking the elevator from the lowly marketer offices to the executive floor.

    It has been revealed that earlier this month, this newsletter noted the trend of holdco CEOs making handshake deals with brand CEOs to poach accounts their agencies didn’t even pitch. That’s the theory behind Publicis landing PepsiCo, Microsoft and LVMH.

    Sources indicate that deloitte Digital is another example, as Digiday reports. The marketing consultancy arm of Deloitte’s holdco is going straight to CEOs to pitch its upcoming enterprise operating system.

    Traditionally, the marketing department has been Deloitte’s target and entry point. But the kind of enterprise deal it’s now seeking requires CEO approval and is part of a “more executive conversation,” claims Deloitte Digital US CMO Mark Singer.

    Plus, Deloitte’s product is called Converge Front Office (or “CFO,” lol).

    The product name is fitting, as Gartner VP Jay Wilson perhaps unwittingly notes, since CFOs are taking bigger roles in evaluating marketing spend: “Increasingly, we see and hear from clients and agencies that the CFO is the critical piece of the new business puzzle, as marketing budgets remain flat.”.

    Deloitte Digital’s thinking is that brands have archives of back-filled content, copy and campaigns that haven’t been touched in ages. So why not have AI agents upcycle that content instead of buying more?

    Gotta hand it to them; it’s definitely not a holdco pitch.

    It’s not just you – the Christmas creep started creeping even earlier this year.

    This September, there were 11% more holiday-themed ads on TV than in 2025 and six times more than in 2021, according to Nielsen.

    Sources indicate that not surprisingly, retailers are on track to spend the most of any ad vertical. They made up almost 64% of all holiday ads aired on linear TV in October, which actually outpaces their usual holiday ad blitz. Over the past five years, retail accounted for about 45% of holiday ads across both linear and streaming TV.

    According to recent reports, nielsen also notes some historical trends that could factor into this holiday season. For instance, there were a lot more automotive holiday ads on streaming (18.4%) than there were on linear (9.7%) last year. Maybe it’s a way to appeal to cord-cutting millennials who’ve started saying “Happy Honda Days” to each other as a bit.

    But does running holiday ads sooner get consumers to spend more throughout the season?

    According to recent reports, according to Deloitte’s annual holiday shopping survey (which was conducted between late August and early September), the average household spend will increase 4% to $1,654 this year. And, while 22% of consumers plan to shop earlier this year, they expect 28% of their budgets to be spent by the end of October – the highest share Deloitte has seen in six years.

    According to recent reports, so total holiday spending may be up a bit. But it won’t pay to wait until Mariah Carey is fully thawed to run those ads.

    Industry observers note that the global internet is getting less global. And questions that once seemed outright crazy – such as, “Might Meta stop doing business in the European Union?” – are not so crazy anymore.

    According to recent reports, there’s no urgent crisis for Meta. The canary in the coal mine is really X. Elon Musk has threatened to stop serving X users in Europe going back to 2023 and fumed over a $140 million Digital Services Act fine last year.

    But as Eric Seufert notes at Mobile Dev Memo, there’s a confluence of problems in Europe for Meta that could force its hand.

    Like X, Meta has also dealt with growing fines from EU regulators. Italy tagged it just yesterday with another billion or so in penalties over privacy violations involving scanned Android camera rolls.

    The EU’s anti-personalization rules and requirement that Meta offer an ad-free subscription service have also decreased the platform’s advertising payouts.

    Plus, the European Commission’s Digital Fairness Act is taking shape. It would prohibit common mobile game monetization tactics like offering virtual in-game currencies or letting owners pay for “variable-reward systems” (aka loot boxes). If mobile games make less money in the EU, that means smaller budgets for mobile app advertising, which is a revenue pillar for Meta.

    Industry observers note that at some point, these things add up. And, eventually, staying in the EU may not make mathematical sense for Meta.

    In a recent development, hearst Magazines launches an agency-esque studio that pairs creators with its editorial brands and advertisers for original content and/or branded campaigns. [Adweek].

    According to recent reports, california sues OpenAI over the Hugging Face incident and other examples of AI agents overstepping their boundaries and escaping research environments. [release].

    Taboola completed its acquisition of Dianomi, a digital ad platform for business, financial services and lifestyle audiences. [release].

    Industry observers note that roughly one in five marketers are trying to quit their jobs – more than double the average for other white collar fields. [Adweek].

    First, email on Thursday, then flights on Friday … on Monday, it was banks reporting technical outages. [Newsweek].

    #32045. Websites Aren’t Just For People Anymore. Here’s How Marketers Optimize Them For Agents

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (694 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Adexchanger ↗ Open Full Page

    Websites Aren’t Just For People Anymore. Here’s How Marketers Optimize Them For Agents

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that it’s always nice for a marketer to get a compliment on their website.
    • Ask again in a few months and we might have an answer.
    • The product builds on its existing AI marketing solution, Ace, but is specifically focused on making website content more accessible to AI agents.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that it’s always nice for a marketer to get a compliment on their website. But does the compliment still resonate when it comes from an AI agent?

    Ask again in a few months and we might have an answer.

    The product builds on its existing AI marketing solution, Ace, but is specifically focused on making website content more accessible to AI agents.

    But what does it mean for content to be accessible to agents that, by definition, can access pretty much all content across the web?

    Effectively, it involves reformatting content into simpler terms and unifying it from multiple sources onto a single webpage, stated Andrew Bolton, chief customer officer at Knotch.

    Most LLM crawlers declare themselves when they access a webpage, so Knotch knows to show them the AI version of a page, said Bolton. For those that don’t declare, Ace can analyze actions like on-site behavior to determine that the viewer is a bot.

    AI agents, unlike humans, don’t care about interactive features or aesthetically pleasing graphics. Instead, their focus is on brevity and direct statements.

    Often, the reformatting includes adding FAQs and concise summaries, as well as removing JavaScript. The result is a pared-down version of the webpage a human would see, but the key content remains.

    Sources indicate that that’s what Bolton describes as a one-to-one version of an existing webpage, in which the information that’s already on it is simply restructured, but nothing new is added. That’s one of the two types of pages that Ace for Agents can develop – the simpler, “v1” offering, remarked Bolton.

    The slightly more advanced version of Ace for Agents involves “injecting new components of information” from other sources of the brand’s choosing, he mentioned, like third-party review sites, or the brand’s own YouTube channel.

    For instance, he added, if a car manufacturer had a particularly favorable review on a third-party site comparing one of its models to a competitor’s model, Knotch can ingest that into the manufacturer’s context model.

    Recent findings suggest that reviews “would be valuable to a consumer who’s trying to evaluate those two different vehicles,” he added. Marketers have a say on whether they want to manually flag external reviews and other content to pull in, or if they want to use an agent to automatically pull in new, positive content, which a human can then review.

    The resulting webpage is a “super piece of content” that is able to “combine the atoms” of several different pages across the web, said Bolton. Now, an LLM only needs to access one page, but gets the same amount of data that it historically would’ve collected from crawling all of the data sources individually.

    Sources indicate that it’s worth noting that the data inputs are entirely curated by the brand. In other words, the good reviews will be ingested, and the bad ones won’t. A brand wouldn’t elect to put negative reviews on their website, Bolton said, and Knotch is effectively creating an agent-readable webpage that pulls all of the informative and positive information on the brand into a single source.

    As marketing and the open web rapidly evolve, agencies need to build an “experience that reaches both the people and the machines,” Melissa Berger, chief solutions officer at Digitas, told AdExchanger. “Earning attention” has always been a major focus for the agency, Berger mentioned, “and now that’s not just earning from the human; it’s earning from the agents, too.”.

    Digitas has been working with Knotch for over a year and began testing Ace for Agents several months ago as a way to earn some of that agentic attention.

    Although Ace for Agents has been a good way for brands to increase discoverability, they still need to understand who their human customers are, remarked Berger. Otherwise, the LLM-accessible site may be full of information, but not have the answers to the specific questions the humans are looking for.

    Once a brand understands exactly what sort of questions its customers are asking and what queries it should aim to show up against, said Berger, “the rest of the content is updated to be catered more toward that.”.

    #32042. Breaking: Ad Tech Doesn’t Need Another Tool. It Needs Fewer Handoffs

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (668 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Adexchanger ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Ad Tech Doesn’t Need Another Tool. It Needs Fewer Handoffs

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (668 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every few months, we get excited about an industry enhancement, like a newly introduced ad format or AI tool.
    • The marketing technology landscape has 15,384 solutions and counting.
    • Think about a typical day for an affiliate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every few months, we get excited about an industry enhancement, like a newly introduced ad format or AI tool. That energy is a big part of what keeps ad tech moving forward, but I believe the next five years will be shaped less by any single innovation and more by how well the tools we already have work together.

    The marketing technology landscape has 15,384 solutions and counting. The opportunity now is in the gaps between them, because that’s where time, data and trust get lost.

    Think about a typical day for an affiliate. They usually juggle several platforms to find offers and buy traffic. And when it comes to site or landing-page monetization, that can mean yet another platform. On top of that, they have to keep track of balances and compare reports.

    Together, these tools power decisions about budgets and traffic. But every handoff takes time, and some data inevitably gets lost along the way.

    Agencies feel it, too. At POSSIBLE earlier this year, the conversation turned to whether AI can finally break down those silos and perhaps eliminate a few steps along the way.

    The most notable handoff in any AI workflow is the one from data to decision. AI can generate advertising copy and visuals very promptly at scale. But it can also optimize areas outside of the creative process: identifying outliers, explaining why a campaign behaves as it does, suggesting improvements, matching traffic with the right offers and taking over repetitive tasks.

    What we don’t discuss enough, however, is that AI is only as good as the data it works with. If the data is flawed or weak, all AI can do is help you make the wrong decision faster. Before automating decisions, it’s worth making sure you can trust the data.

    Some of the riskiest handoffs are the ones we don’t control at all, especially our dependence on platforms that can change the rules overnight.

    Sources indicate that in February, Google removed parked domains from its Search Partner Network, and a long-established monetization model suddenly became much harder to rely on. Last year, Chrome started automatically revoking notification permissions from sites if consumers ignore them. And, notably, Google’s decision to retire key Privacy Sandbox APIs showed how uncertain it is to wait for one substantial replacement.

    Sources indicate that changes like these will keep coming. However, there is something we can do: Build businesses that adapt rapidly. When the parked-domain change happened, RollerAds didn’t start from scratch; we adapted the traffic monetization infrastructure we already had to work with domain traffic. In my experience, that’s what most real innovation looks like: spotting a shift early and building on what you already do well.

    The last handoff is between partners, and it only works if both sides trust what they’re seeing.

    Advertisers need to trust their partner platform and the traffic this platform provides. Publishers need to be able to predict their earnings. Affiliates need their conversions reported accurately. A great interface makes all of this easier to see, but what earns trust is what’s underneath: reliable tracking, fraud protection and clear, honest communication.

    If I could ask the industry for one thing, it would be to make ad tech understandable.

    At its core, the idea of digital advertising is simple: Show people relevant ads. But, over time, it has grown into a complex mix of acronyms, integrations and dashboards.

    Here’s my invitation to every platform: Before shipping the next feature, count the handoffs it removes. That’s the thinking behind RollerAds as a full-cycle ad platform. We’ve brought buying traffic, monetizing sites and running offers together in one account, and we keep looking for more steps to remove. The next significant thing in ad tech may not be a thing at all. It will be the stage when tools combine into one seamless process with fewer handoffs, data we can trust, businesses that can absorb change and partners who make hard things simpler.

    We can start building it today.

    Disney Touts Its Streaming Success In Latest Earnings

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After a lot of internal upheaval and consolidation, the House of Mouse finds itself in a pretty good place going into its fiscal 2027 year.
    • Sources indicate that so states upcoming CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston during an earnings call on Tuesday.
    • For the full year, revenue not only increased 8% but broke the $100 billion mark, from $94 billion in the fiscal year 2025 to $102.3 billion in 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After a lot of internal upheaval and consolidation, the House of Mouse finds itself in a pretty good place going into its fiscal 2027 year.

    Sources indicate that so states upcoming CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston during an earnings call on Tuesday. They told investors that Disney exceeded its guidance for the previous quarter and is on track to exceed its three-year adjusted earnings-per-share growth guidance going into the new year.

    For the full year, revenue not only increased 8% but broke the $100 billion mark, from $94 billion in the fiscal year 2025 to $102.3 billion in 2026.

    Meanwhile, for Disney’s Q4 (the company starts its fiscal year a quarter earlier), revenue increased 16% to $25.9 billion for last quarter, compared to $22.5 the year before.

    Within entertainment, advertising grew 10% to $1.7 billion. And SVOD revenue increased 19% to $6.1 billion, with 22% subscription revenue growth.

    You’re watching Disney Channel!

    In TV, D’Amaro highlighted the critical buzz around Hulu’s crime thriller “Furious,” high ratings for the fresh season of “Dancing with the Stars” and excitement over “The Remarried Empress,” a South Korean romantasy that debuted as the biggest premiere for a local original across Disney+ and Hulu globally. The latter is indicative of Disney’s proposal to invest more in international content, a strategy that’s been working wonders for competitors like Netflix.

    In a recent development, sports are also a significant deal, of course. Subscription and affiliate fee revenue in the sports segment increased 18% in the quarter to $3.4 billion, with advertising revenue growth of 20%.

    According to recent reports, disney will continue to grow its sports footprint next year with expanded college football rights, increased “Monday Night Football” ratings and ESPN’s first ever Super Bowl telecast. (Well, technically, it’s ABC’s turn to host the Substantial Game, but it’ll also be cross-broadcast on other Disney channels.).

    Where Disney’s overall streaming strategy is concerned, D’Amaro told investors that there will be a larger focus on “connecting services” – which includes other nonentertainment sides of the business like parks, cruise ships and merchandise.

    More practically, though, “connecting services” means finally unifying Disney+ and Hulu into one app, which D’Amaro stated would start in December. It also means adding more sports content to Disney+ and introducing creator content from TikTok into the Disney+ mobile app next month. The move might strike some as strange, but given that ESPN’s short-form Verts product broke records in September and October, maybe there’s something to it.

    At the same time, Disney is still exploring the idea of a free streaming product, which leadership first discussed during last quarter’s earnings reports.

    Despite – or maybe because of – all the streaming success, Disney revealed it will stop reporting its SVOD operating income beginning next quarter. At the same time, the company will also provide additional disclosures related to revenue within the entertainment segment.

    SVOD revenues will still be reported, Johnston clarified to investors, but so will content and IP revenues. Revenue for linear networks will be combined with the virtual MVPD business.

    The goal, noted Johnston, is to provide investors with “additional information and a better lens into our content monetization,” while allowing Disney’s team more flexibility to “invest appropriately” in growing SVOD.

    In other words, Disney’s likely planning to spend a lot more money on its SVOD business – and maybe it doesn’t want investors to worry too much about how the sausage is getting made.

    All aboard Consolidation Station.

    Disney’s remarkable growth this past quarter isn’t surprising, given how much the company has restructured since D’Amaro took on the CEO role in March. At least 1,000 members of Disney’s workforce have been laid off since then, with more job cuts and consolidation reportedly on the way.

    All that streamlining is expected to translate into $3 billion in run rate savings by 2029, according to D’Amaro.

    To highlight the ways Disney is prioritizing efficiency and consolidation, D’Amaro also shouted out the firm’s first ever chief technology officer, Karandeep Anand, who came from the (now bankrupt) chatbot startup Character.ai.

    Recent findings suggest that not surprisingly, Disney aims to continue investing in AI tools and technology across its entire business, even parks. Although D’Amaro didn’t bring up the tech giant’s recent purchase of Character.ai’s assets, he did hype up how the tech is being used in the streaming side of the business, both within Disney+’s content recommendation engine and in the advertising products Disney makes available to its marketing clients.

    According to recent reports, in addition to Disney’s AI creative studio that uses existing brand material to develop CTV-ready ads, the organization also released an agentic ad campaign tool in August. Both were previewed at its tech and data showcase at CES earlier this year.

    Now, almost half of all fresh ad campaigns are flowing through the agentic tool, according to Disney’s ad sales team.

    • It is easy to get seduced by the promise of hyper-targeting in connected TV.
    • But stacking audience filters—like trying to reach “hang-gliding nuns who drink energy drinks”—creates a massive problem for local advertisers: it shrinks the available pool of households down to virtually zero.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Premion’s Head of Pricing and Planning, Adolfo Arbulú, on why hyper-targeting suffocates local CTV campaigns, and why AI still requires a human in the lead.

    It is easy to get seduced by the promise of hyper-targeting in connected TV.

    But stacking audience filters—like trying to reach “hang-gliding nuns who drink energy drinks”—creates a massive problem for local advertisers: it shrinks the available pool of households down to virtually zero.

    In this episode of Inside the Stack, Premion’s Head of Pricing & Planning, Adolfo Arbulú, joins the podcast to untangle the Local CTV Paradox.

    He explains why true precision actually depends on scale, and why chasing that scale across multiple unmanaged CTV partners creates massive frequency overlap and hidden waste.

    In a recent development, we also dig into the reality of AI in local markets. For a local campaign generating a few dozen conversions a week, relying on hourly AI optimization simply creates noise.

    Arbulú also shared why campaign measurement must be decided well before the buy, how Premion is using a proprietary identity graph to control frequency, and why navigating local nuances—like unexpected town layoffs or mid-term political cycles—means AI still desperately needs a human in the lead.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    YouTube has become TV, video podcasts are following suit and now Meta is looking for its way into the living room.

    In a recent development, meta has already been testing Instagram for TV built around long-form creator content. But it could make a bigger splash in the TV world through the acquisition of a CTV startup or a streaming company so Reels are “front and center on TV screens,” Mike Shields suggests in his Next in Media Substack.

    In a recent development, if Meta wants to compete with Google and Amazon, acquiring, owning and operating are probably paramount (no pun intended). “Audience alone won’t be enough,” Dan Larkman, CEO and founder of performance CTV tech company Keynes, tells Shields.

    But others argue that bringing Instagram to TV doesn’t require acquisitions – just Meta investing to build out its own existing features.

    According to recent reports, and perhaps Meta agrees. According to Shields, citing sources familiar with the discussions, Meta is talking with TV OEMs and FAST platforms about adding an “extend to CTV” option to its ad-buying platform.

    Speaking of TV, Fubo’s quarterly earnings report card was a mixed bag.

    The sports-centric streamer saw overall revenue inch up ever so slightly to $1.5 billion last quarter, compared with $1.48 billion during the same period last year. But it suffered a heavy net loss of $51.8 million last quarter, compared with $38.8 million a year ago.

    It has been revealed that the streamer blames operational and restructuring costs related to its recent merger with Hulu + Live TV for most of its recent losses. Going forward, it’s betting on advertising and live sports distribution (surprise, surprise!) to save the day under its upcoming CEO Alisa Bowen.

    And ad revenue is already moving in the right direction.

    Sources indicate that bowen also told investors that the company looks to keep aggregating sports content rather than investing in sports rights, which are not getting any cheaper. However, some analysts believe that content IP ownership – including for sports – is more valuable as a competitive differentiator compared with distributed content. (Ruh-roh.).

    Guess sports alone aren’t enough to keep Wall Street happy.

    Recent findings suggest that the internet opened up access to information. AI is helping significant platforms close it back down.

    Google is starting to put up barriers to its search results. It’s testing a prompt that asks people to sign in to verify they’re human, Search Engine Roundtable reports. The prompt appears when Google suspects a bot is scraping its results.

    According to recent reports, the same barriers are appearing on Google Maps and business reviews, since reviews contain such rich data on particular products and customer intent. Meanwhile, OpenAI has done the same thing with its results so rival bots can’t scrape and reverse engineer its outputs.

    In a recent development, oh, and Meta is running campaigns to get people to download Muse, its AI agent, as a Chrome extension. This could help Muse get around bot detection tools used by publishers and retailers like Amazon and eBay.

    Finally, Reddit was built around the notion of transparency and free access, so it was a big change last month when it removed public API access and the free feed.

    According to recent reports, A hack of website experimentation platform Optimizely resulted in site visitors being exposed to credit card skimmers and iOS exploit kits across sites owned by 178 major organizations, including Salesforce, CNN, BBC and Zoom. [blog].

    Industry observers note that who even qualifies as a creator, anyway? [Digiday].

    Nvidia confirms a new committee focused on national security and export controls. Better late than never. [The Information].

    Attain is the inaugural data partner in The Trade Desk’s new Open Measurement product. [release].

    The FBI flags Gootloader, a malware campaign that used more than 1,000 compromised WordPress sites and SEO tricks to lure users into downloading malware disguised as business documents. [Search Engine Roundtable].

    Instagram (finally) lets creators add Amazon affiliate links directly to Reels and feed posts. [TechCrunch].

    Erin Foxworthy, a Snowflake VP and its global head of industry, media and entertainment, joins the IAB Tech Lab board. [post].

    Melanie Zimmermann joins Kroger Precision Marketing from Criteo as group VP. [release].

    Creative agency Saylor appoints Sarah McMains as chief strategy officer. [release].

    Team Dayā, a nonprofit founded by ad tech industry vets that funds and builds primary schools in remote, developing regions, has hired Isabella Winkler as its first executive director. [release].

    Tech Report: Philips Sonicare Polishes Its Streaming TV Strategy Using Amazon Ads Agent

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brushing your teeth is a chore, and so is trying to buy streaming TV ad inventory publisher by publisher.
    • According to recent reports, during the 2025-26 upfront season, Philips Sonicare, a maker of electric toothbrushes and water flossers, decided to consolidate its streaming TV ad buys within Amazon, which has also been doing some consolidating itself.
    • It has been revealed that in both cases, the rationale for consolidation is simplification.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brushing your teeth is a chore, and so is trying to buy streaming TV ad inventory publisher by publisher.

    According to recent reports, during the 2025-26 upfront season, Philips Sonicare, a maker of electric toothbrushes and water flossers, decided to consolidate its streaming TV ad buys within Amazon, which has also been doing some consolidating itself. Amazon recently centralized its Amazon DSP has been replaced by a latest product called DVA (which stands for “display, video and audio”).

    It has been revealed that in both cases, the rationale for consolidation is simplification. When media workflows merge, ad transactions need fewer dashboards and third parties, which improves campaign efficiency and performance.

    Philips Sonicare, which was already using Amazon’s Sponsored Ads to market its products on the flagship site, but wanted to expand its target audience after finding that 86% of the oral care audience segment was not considering Philips products.

    To reach them, the brand paired Amazon’s data with its own first-party data to create custom audience segments of customers who are in market for oral care products but haven’t shopped from Philips before.

    As part of its upfront commitment, Philips used Amazon Ads Agent to buy streaming media across Paramount+, Roku, Tubi, Peacock, TelevisaUnivision and Warner Bros. Discovery. Previously, it had to work with each of these publishers separately.

    By consolidating its buys, Philips saw 24% incremental reach it saw among audiences likely to be interested in its products, as well as a 75% reduction in customer cost per acquisition.

    For brands, centralizing multi-platform streaming buys improves visibility across channels, which helps advertisers learn more about their audience and adjust their campaigns accordingly.

    “By working with Amazon Ads to consolidate our streaming TV investment, we can apply one audience strategy across our portfolio, and manage reach and frequency more effectively while better understanding what happens after an ad is seen,” Priyanti Telang, director of Amazon activation, retail media and digital shelf excellence for Philips North America, told me.

    Using one buying platform also helps Philips speed up reporting.

    Buying media and pulling reports from several platforms is “highly inefficient” because there is audience overlap, said Chris Conetta, director of omnichannel supply for Amazon Ads, so marketers “lose a lot of the incrementality you get when using one tool that can measure audiences across multiple touchpoints.”.

    Industry observers note that that logic applies beyond just Amazon’s platform. Amazon (and other retailers, for that matter) can also attract brands seeking more purchase data to improve their performance and attribution, including on streaming TV.

    Since TV is in its performance era, it’s not surprising that Philips was keen to prove streaming’s impact.

    One of the clearest findings from its media consolidation effort, Telang mentioned, is that “streaming can generate measurable intent.” After seeing the brand’s connected TV ads, more consumers searched online for Philips products by name, she said, and “that intent translated into purchases.”.

    Philips saw a 15x higher purchase rate among consumers who saw the ads on streaming TV than among consumers who only saw a Sponsored Ads placement for Philips online.

    Conetta noted, however, that this increase was a result of customers seeing Philips ads across both streaming and on Amazon’s site. An Amazon executive would say that, but Conetta has a point. Industry research suggests that diversified ad formats can drive improved brand results.

    Philips Sonicare’s experience also notes something about streaming TV’s place in the marketing funnel, Telang said, “as a contributor to commercial performance as well as brand awareness.” Guess reach and performance complement each other like brushing and flossing.

    In other words, brace yourselves (ha) to hear more about “full-funnel” advertising in CTV advertising discussions.

    Putting AI To Work At WSJ

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The best AI use cases in ad sales aren’t flashy.
    • That’s been the case at The Wall Street Journal, where AI is quietly taking over most of the busywork for the ad sales team, notes Josh Stinchcomb, the Journal’s global CRO, on this week’s episode of AdExchanger Talks.
    • For example, what seller doesn’t know the frustration of trying to track down a stat buried somewhere in an old email thread or Slack channel when they’re trying to get ready for a meeting?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The best AI use cases in ad sales aren’t flashy. Mostly, it’s about automating the tasks nobody wanted to do anyway.

    That’s been the case at The Wall Street Journal, where AI is quietly taking over most of the busywork for the ad sales team, notes Josh Stinchcomb, the Journal’s global CRO, on this week’s episode of AdExchanger Talks.

    For example, what seller doesn’t know the frustration of trying to track down a stat buried somewhere in an old email thread or Slack channel when they’re trying to get ready for a meeting?

    But now, the Journal’s sales team has access to an internal AI-powered search tool that does the digging for them. It can even recap whatever the seller last discussed with a particular prospect so they can walk into their meeting prepared and knowing exactly where the conversation left off.

    “It’s really helpful for pulling from the information we have available to ourselves but isn’t always at our fingertips,” Stinchcomb claims. “That’s been a great time-saver.”.

    There’s also a tool for digital ops that checks line items against ad creative and IOs and also handles taking campaign screenshots, which Stinchcomb describes as a decidedly “laborious and really unfun” task. The result, he notes, is fewer botched campaign debuts and less inventory lost to make-goods.

    But the bigger bet is media planning.

    Sources indicate that right now, it takes a planner four or five hours to turn an RFP into a proposal, Stinchcomb notes, in part because they have to check inventory across multiple different systems. The Journal is testing a tool, however, that can read RFPs, look at past campaigns for similar audiences and build a recommended plan in about an hour.

    In a recent development, with the team producing thousands of looks a year, that’s a lot of hours back in their lives. The time and effort saved is being redeployed toward larger million-dollar-plus RFPs, where Stinchcomb says the Journal’s win rate has gone up five percentage points. A wider rollout of the tool is planned for early next year.

    According to recent reports, “Bringing it all together is a great strategy,” he claims. “It’s an efficient way to bring in chunks of revenue.”.

    It has been revealed that but there’s one place where AI isn’t welcome, though, and that’s in the writing of branded content, which is a growing business for the Journal. WSJ Intelligence, its custom content studio, takes its cue from the Journal’s newsroom. The work might be “facilitated by these tools,” Stinchcomb notes, “but not written by them.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “AI is great at sort of rehashing what’s out there,” Stinchcomb notes. “It’s not necessarily great at breaking news, as it were, or bringing a fresher perspective.”.

    Branded content has to be as interesting and engaging as anything else that’s out there competing for a reader’s attention.

    And if it commits the sin of being boring or derivative, Stinchcomb says, then “[people] don’t read it, and I’m not getting paid.”.

    Also in this episode: Why less than 5% of the Journal’s digital ad revenue is programmatic, how WSJ Intelligence keeps its custom research credible, News Corp’s “woo and sue” approach to AI licensing deals and Stinchcomb’s past life as the singer in a “tragic emo-style” band in high school.

    #32031. Canvas Worldwide’s Agentic Layer Helps Zillow Distinguish Real Renters From Dreamers

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (884 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Adexchanger ↗ Open Full Page

    Canvas Worldwide’s Agentic Layer Helps Zillow Distinguish Real Renters From Dreamers

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We’ve all been there: You look up a product out of sheer curiosity with no intent to actually spend money on it, and suddenly you’re inundated with ads for similar products.
    • The challenge for advertisers is distinguishing the passive browsers from the people with genuine purchase intent.
    • In a recent development, zillow knows that challenge well.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We’ve all been there: You look up a product out of sheer curiosity with no intent to actually spend money on it, and suddenly you’re inundated with ads for similar products.

    The challenge for advertisers is distinguishing the passive browsers from the people with genuine purchase intent.

    In a recent development, zillow knows that challenge well. Its rental site often serves as a place for people to fantasize about their future home, even if they’re not actually looking to move.

    In a recent development, “We are known for dreaming,” said Ravi Kandikonda, SVP of marketing for Zillow Group. But that’s not necessarily a bad thing. Welcoming the dreamers is a great way for Zillow to drive awareness of its brand and get potential future renters into its platform, Kandikonda added. From there, it’s a matter of striking a balance between building awareness and driving conversions.

    That’s where Zillow turns to its media agency partner, Canvas Worldwide.

    Sources indicate that in September, Canvas announced a newly introduced division called ART Dept., which provides a collection of AI solutions to help brands and agencies optimize their campaign budgeting and pacing. Zillow is using ART Dept.’s AI agents to better separate the renters from the dreamers and tailor its marketing accordingly.

    According to recent reports, the “ART” in ART Dept. stands for “AI Applied Research and Technology.” (Though, if we’re being pedantic, wouldn’t that be AART – or AIART?).

    Quibbles about acronyms aside, Canvas’ latest division offers a mix of AI optimization features that are becoming commonplace for ad agencies and marketing platforms. Though, like other agentic platforms, Canvas states its differentiation comes from how it applies those optimizations to its agentic layer.

    For example, offering a pacing dashboard is “table stakes” by now, rather than a distinguishing feature for an agency, said Sally Lee, SVP of programmatic and ART at Canvas.

    But Canvas wanted to make its pacing dashboard “multidimensional” by connecting it with a budget source of truth and building an agentic layer on top of it, stated Lee.

    In a recent development, the agentic layer, called Talos, determines whether a campaign is underpacing or overpacing and optimizes for better performance. Before pushing the newly optimized campaign into the platform, a member of the Canvas team reviews and approves (or denies) it.

    Canvas can “pick and choose from different search and behavioral categories” to optimize against, noted Lee. In Zillow’s case, that might include whether a user is researching renter’s insurance or looking into moving truck rentals.

    Canvas gets those behavioral signals through its data partnerships, including its MCP connection to predictive audience targeting organization Dstillery.

    Access to behavioral data has helped Zillow reach more specific audiences and be smarter about exactly where and when to target them, said Kandikonda.

    For instance, targeting multifamily renters in Seattle using a generic, off-the-shelf “multifamily apartment buildings” audience only goes so far, he noted. “I need to know when they are on a particular platform” to bid for that audience at the right moment with the right content, he added.

    Dstillery’s audience modeling predicts which websites the target audience will visit and when based on real behavioral data. And Canvas’ AI can help surface audience and behavioral overlaps that might have previously gone overlooked by its team.

    Canvas’ reliance on data-backed reasoning was a major draw for Zillow when the two first started working together in 2023, Kandikonda said, and it continues to be a major focus of ART Dept.

    The goal behind the newly introduced product suite is to save media teams time figuring out what media is performing and how much to spend on different audience segments.

    According to recent reports, increasing ROI is crucial for any brand. But it’s particularly important within the real estate market, Kandikonda stated, as marketing dollars are constrained and the entire industry “is bouncing around the box.”.

    So, while Zillow appreciates its dreamer audience, it’s feeling the same pressure most brands are to focus on lower-funnel conversions, such as “actual movers,” Kandikonda said.

    That’s part of the reason off-the-shelf renter audiences weren’t cutting it for Zillow’s ads business, he added.

    According to recent reports, an off-the-shelf audience may indicate people who are interested in renting more broadly, he noted, but ART was able to select for people who were actively in the process of planning a move. And more precise targeting means better lower-funnel ad performance.

    The destination, not the journey.

    From Zillow’s perspective, the biggest change from using Canvas’ ART Dept. is the results, rather than the process. After all, the AI tools are used by the Canvas team, rather than by Zillow.

    Zillow just tells Canvas what outcome it wants to achieve. Canvas then translates the desired outcome into a scorecard that weights different goals and metrics within the interoperable tech infrastructure that powers the ART Dept., which is called +Suite.

    Industry observers note that from there, Canvas’ Audience+ product (which is similar to a data management platform) connects to data partners and the Talos AI agent to build custom audiences. Finally, Talos activates and optimizes the campaign.

    The system creates an ongoing feedback loop, noted Canvas’ Lee: “Build an audience, activate it, see how it’s performing against what that client cares about and identify where to make changes to drive a better outcome.”.

    Create a visceral experience that translates into emotions of inspiration, awe from users.

    Use a Science-backed, Cinematic, Contrarian style : Every product touchpoint should be grounded in behavioral science, expressed with cinematic beauty, and challenge conventions.

    -----------------------------------------.

    3–6 years as a Product Manager / Product Owner in EdTech, SaaS, or Consumer Tech.

    Bonus: experience in AI-driven products, learning design, or personal development platforms.

    You’ve shipped at least one major feature or product end-to-end, and can show measurable results.

    Uses Figma comfortably, prototypes directly.

    Craft-obsessed : You get things done, you love to work much beyond 9-5, you have a doer mentality, a bias for outcomes and want to be a beast in your field.

    User & Impact Obsessed: You think in outcomes, not outputs, you care about transformation.

    Analytical & System Thinker: You can turn a vague problem into a clear hypothesis, metrics, and roadmap.

    Digital & AI savvy : you’re able to build AI Agents (if not, you demonstrate ability to learn while applying).

    Cross-disciplinary Curiosity: You speak both tech and human; You can move from vision to spreadsheet to Figma.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    Our chosen language for written communication is English.

    --------------------------------.

    ❌ If you need clarity before chaos — wrong place.❌ If you prefer balance over intensity — wrong season.❌ If you build to deliver, not to elevate — wrong mission.

    Recent findings suggest that ❌Surface-level Vision Alignment : you like the idea of Paradox but doesn’t want to get the depth. Paradox is design-led; you must touch the product, not just manage it.

    ✅ If you’re obsessed with systems, psychology, and design…✅ If you dream of using AI to amplify what makes us human….

    Build a product that fuses neuroscience, design, and AI to reinvent how humans grow.

    The chance to build a product that could redefine human potential.

    Work with filmmakers, psychologists, engineers, and creatives obsessed with impact.

    In the heart of our headquarters stands the 100 000 Dreams Wall,.

    Every photo on that wall is a life rewritten:.

    “I found peace with my father.”.

    You will play a crucial role in the development of an Iconic Product.

    -> 🏅Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform.

    But you don’t just want a competitive paycheck, you also want….

    -> Playing a crucial role in the development of a manufacturer whose content and products will be used by millions of people.

    -> Waking up in the morning feeling like you are making a difference is something!We receive messages every day from clients who have successfully lost weight, quit smoking, reached a milestone in their business, built better relationships, and made positive changes in their lives.

    -> ❤️ Contributing to the Paradox Foundation (our non-profit), dedicated to empower teenagers.

    But that's not all, we believe that driven people deserve….

    -> 😎A organization culture based on autonomy & accountability.

    -> 🌎A remote culture from day one with the freedom to work from wherever you want.

    -> 🏤Magnificent office in Dubai, Paris, Lisbon - it feels like home :).

    -> 🧍‍♀️Standing desks paid by the company if you live far from our offices.

    -> 💻Work on Mac, for us it counts :).

    -> 🏀350€ per year paid by the company to take care of yourself ( for your gym, or dance class or whatever make you feel great).

    -> 📚150€ of books or education - At Paradox, we are learner lovers and we want to support you in that.

    -> 🔥6 1:1coachings - A Paradox Coach supporting you on anything personal or professional, we want you to live your best life.

    ⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this : do not apply ⚠️.

    If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀🚀🚀.

    That job description resonated with you?

    Here is your tailor made hiring process.

    📃 A 6 to 8 minutes application survey (with a short video assignment).

    💻 A 30mn video call with Timy, HR, to deep dive into your career path and ambitions.

    💻 A 1h video call with Timy, HR, to discuss how you'd fit into Paradox’s Product team.

    💻 A 1h culture-fit video call, to assess alignment with our values and mindset.

    💻 A 1h final video call with David, CEO, to discuss Product Vision and the next milestones to build.

    💼 Reference check to understand how you operate across environments and help set you up for a smooth onboarding.

    It has been revealed that our recruitment process is tailored to do our best to avoid that you or us realize that we’re not a perfect fit. Every step serves a purpose and will allow us to get to know you better as much as it’ll help you understand more where you’ll be stepping in.

    We also want you to have time to ask all of your questions regarding the mission, the long-term vision of your team and the tech giant, our values, with the relevant interlocutor in front of you.

    If you believe design and AI can awaken what’s best in us then this isn’t a career move.

    Let’s build the Operating System for Greatness.

    Senior Product Builder - Hub at Camunda

    📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1356 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes.
    • According to recent reports, camunda Hub is where enterprises run Camunda at scale.
    • Take over Hub's fleet propagation mechanism from the team building its first version, and make it work for access, secrets, tenants, licences and custom roles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

    According to recent reports, camunda Hub is where enterprises run Camunda at scale. From Hub they manage their clusters and tenants, decide who can do what, and roll changes out across the whole organization. We’re looking for a Senior Product Builder to own the backend and architecture that let Hub manage a whole fleet of clusters. Your first focus will be the mechanism that sends access, secret, tenant and licence changes out to every connected cluster and brings deployments, health and audit records back. From there, you’ll shape Hub’s foundations: its event model, the service boundaries and data model other teams build on, and how Hub behaves when things fail or get upgraded. The platform is your product. Your customers are platform administrators, Centres of Excellence and the builders across Camunda who depend on what you create. You’ll join a latest two-person pod in our remote-first team. You’ll have real ownership as the person who makes the call, and you’ll build AI-first, from written specs through to production. Our customers run mission-critical processes on Camunda, so your work will matter to them every day.

    Take over Hub's fleet propagation mechanism from the team building its first version, and make it work for access, secrets, tenants, licences and custom roles.

    Write short design documents for foundational changes, get them reviewed by the teams that depend on them, and turn them into tested, shipped code.

    Design how Hub behaves when things go wrong: offline clusters, partial failures, Hub outages, and clusters being adopted or detached.

    Build the path from clusters back to Hub, starting with deployment inventory, health, audit records and licence status.

    Design Hub's first event and webhook mechanism, so admins and agents can react to changes instead of polling for them.

    Join the pod's rotations and Hub on-call, and help other builders take on backend work through reviews, guidelines and contract tests.

    What You Will Bring to the Role:.

    Experience building and running backend systems in production that other teams or customers depend on.

    Comfort taking a problem nobody owns yet and turning it into a design, a blueprint and shipped code.

    Product judgment for technical users: you talk to the people who use your APIs and make trade-offs on their behalf.

    Clear, short writing that lets a remote team review and decide asynchronously.

    Care for how a system behaves when parts of it fail, not only for the happy path.

    Industry observers note that designed and shipped a control plane or similar system that pushes desired state to many targets. Knows outbox or event-log patterns, idempotent apply, versioning, retries and drift reconciliation.

    Senior backend engineering in Java (API design, relational data models, multi-tenant SaaS services) and hands-on Helm and Kubernetes for self-managed installations.

    Sources indicate that software architecture and failure analysis: partial failure, blast radius, consistency trade-offs. Has debugged production incidents in a distributed system and is ready for on-call.

    According to recent reports, has shaped an API or platform as a product, and writes design docs other teams can build on. Gets agreement across teams without formal authority.

    Builds AI-first from written specifications and checks AI output as carefully as any other code.

    Kubernetes operators or GitOps tools, for example Argo CD.

    OIDC, SCIM and permission models, or secret managers and licence systems.

    Camunda 8 or another workflow or orchestration engine.

    Enough frontend skill to build a thin UI on top of a backend capability.

    This role is an existing vacancy.

    #LI-AM1 #LI-Remote #C1 #USEAST #USWEST.

    Industry observers note that we offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition.

    The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills, experience, and location, and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth:.

    United States: $143,800.00 to $231,900.00.

    United Kingdom: £90,300.00 to £148,500.00.

    Singapore: S$178,600.00 to S$267,900.00.

    Canada: C$152,700.00 to C$251,200.

    If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview.

    Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Strategy (VSOP).

    Sources indicate that we invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable.

    Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it.

    In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets, including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi.

    In a recent development, health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program releases in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

    Financial Security: Retirement and pension plans (often with company contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant.

    Professional Growth: Up to $/€/£1,000 per year for self-driven learning: courses, certifications, books, you decide!

    According to recent reports, AI in our hiring process: Camunda may use AI tools to aid the screening of applications and during the interview process. You can learn more here.

    ”Everyone is welcome at Camunda” — it’s a celebrated component of our culture. We strive to create an inclusive environment that empowers our people. At Camunda, we honour diverse cultures and backgrounds and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, belief, sexual orientation, age, disability or any other protected characteristics under applicable law. We are looking forward to your application!

    Come join us and be part of Camunda’s incredible journey: Make an impact at a pivotal moment in our story!

    Please be aware that scammers may impersonate Camunda by reaching out about job opportunities. Camunda will only contact candidates from an email address ending in @camunda.com or @talent.camunda.com. We will never ask candidates for bank account details, checks, payment, or other sensitive financial information as part of our hiring process. If you receive a suspicious message, please do not respond, click any links, or share personal information.

    By opting in to SMS use, please be aware that:.

    Text message frequency may vary;.

    Standard text message and data rates may apply; and.

    By opting in, you will be enrolled directly in ongoing recruiting text messages from Camunda.

    According to recent reports, to opt-out, simply select 'No' when prompted during your application. You can also change your preferences at any time by contacting talent-operations@camunda.com.

    Latest report claims TikTok Live is fastest-growing platform for game streaming

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (397 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As TwitchCon descends upon San Diego, a different hub for video game streaming is celebrating its ascendance.
    • Hatchet (previously known as Stream Hatchet) dispensed its TikTok Live status report as part of a biannual enhancement related to the ByteDance-owned platform.
    • Previous Hatchet reports have characterized Twitch and YouTube Gaming‘s dominant positions within the streaming landscape, but the firm’s latest dispatches have shown that TikTok Live is gaining on its market-leading rivals.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As TwitchCon descends upon San Diego, a different hub for video game streaming is celebrating its ascendance. TikTok Live is the fastest growing platform in that category, according to a latest report published by the GameSquare subsidiary Hatchet.

    Hatchet (previously known as Stream Hatchet) dispensed its TikTok Live status report as part of a biannual enhancement related to the ByteDance-owned platform. During the first half of 2026, gaming streams on TikTok Live pulled in 2.5 billion hours of watch time. That traffic gave TikTok Live a 14% share of the game streaming market, pulling it even with the Stake.com-affiliated platform Kick.

    Previous Hatchet reports have characterized Twitch and YouTube Gaming‘s dominant positions within the streaming landscape, but the firm’s latest dispatches have shown that TikTok Live is gaining on its market-leading rivals. While TikTok Live watch time grew 96% year-over-year, Twitch and YouTube Gaming’s respective market shares both went down.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Through properties like Hatchet, FaZe Clan, and TubeBuddy, GameSquare has made deep inroads in digital gaming communities. “Hatchet’s latest report demonstrates just how rapidly TikTok Live has established itself in gaming live-streaming,” remarked GameSquare CEO Justin Kenna in a statement. “Nearly doubling its gaming hours watched in a year is a clear signal that audience habits are shifting toward mobile, discovery-driven viewing.”.

    According to recent reports, kenna cited titles like Roblox, Garena Free Fire, and Mobile Legends as three major drivers of TikTok Live’s watch time uptick. Roblox led all games in terms of TikTok Live watch time during the first half of 2026; it generated 631 million hours of TikTok viewership during that period.

    Roblox is a favorite of Gen Alpha gamers, while Free Fire and Mobile Legends appeal to gamers on mobile devices, especially outside of the United States. Those two data points help explain how TikTok Live has managed such a sizable gaming glow-up — it has volume none of its competitors can match. With 1.4 million creators active each day, TikTok Live’s community is nearly twice as big as Twitch’s.

    That massive quantity has made TikTok Live a market leader across multiple streaming categories. Its gaming operation, however, is one of its strongest fortes, and rival platforms should be prepared to see more growth from their ByteDance-owned competitor.

    #32013. The $4 million Internet Invitational might become golf’s next substantial thing — or another bogey

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (548 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tubefilter ↗ Open Full Page

    The $4 million Internet Invitational might become golf’s next substantial thing — or another bogey

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • You could make the case that the most exciting golf event of 2026 involved a majority of amateurs and average joes — and the PGA wasn’t involved in the planning at all.
    • The driving force behind the Internet Invitational is Dave Portnoy, the provocateur and pizza lover who is best known as the owner of Barstool Sports.
    • Recent findings suggest that the first Internet Invitational, organized in 2025, featured Dunkin as a sponsor and a $1 million prize.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You could make the case that the most exciting golf event of 2026 involved a majority of amateurs and average joes — and the PGA wasn’t involved in the planning at all. I’m talking about the Internet Invitational, which recently wrapped up its second season by splitting a $4 million prize among the 16 members of the winning team.

    The driving force behind the Internet Invitational is Dave Portnoy, the provocateur and pizza lover who is best known as the owner of Barstool Sports. To create an event that could demonstrate the influence and appeal of the “YouTube golf” scene, Portnoy teamed up with Robby Berger and his Bob Does Sports brand.

    Recent findings suggest that the first Internet Invitational, organized in 2025, featured Dunkin as a sponsor and a $1 million prize. The event was put on as a response to the PGA’s uneven investment in golf personalities. The Creator Classic that had signaled the PGA’s interest in digital partnerships was not held at TPC Sawgrass in 2026.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Sources indicate that portnoy and Berger bet that they could outdo the PGA by fully embracing golf creators, and they doubled down in 2026, when they quadrupled the size of the Internet Invitational prize. “It’s all because of Dave, man,” Barstool Sports video editor Brendan Jones told Golf magazine. “Dave puts up all this money, and that changes people. That’s not good or bad — it just changes the way that people act, right? Dave’s major thing with anything that we do at Barstool, it’s like, what are the stakes? Why do people care? How are we going to get anything out of them?”.

    According to recent reports, in this case, people care because the proceedings were sillier, wackier, and more relatable than anything a PGA-sanctioned event could deliver. There were breakout stars like Paige Spiranac, wildly varied handicaps, and plenty of substance use during the tournament. And the fans loved it. Viewership hit 3.5 million during the first 24 hours and ballooned past 11 million views within a week.

    In a recent development, “When you put the average Joe, who’s not a great golfer— that, to I think a lot of people, was riveting,” Berger told The Hollywood Reporter. “I mean, it’s kind of what Bob Does Sports was built off of.”.

    In a recent development, as exciting as the action may have been, the Internet Invitational wasn’t free from drama. Nelk member Salim Sirur‘s excessive drinking and Sam Heung Min‘s criticisms related to rules enforcement added controversy to the event’s conclusion. Given Portnoy’s controversial past and the indiscretions of some big names in the YouTube golf community (looking at you, Good Good), one wonders how long the Internet Invitational can sustain its positive momentum.

    But the success of the tournament’s second iteration can’t be ignored. With the decline of LIV Golf and the presence of elite golfers on YouTube, there’s an opportunity for creators to build a viable alternative to the PGA Tour. To do that will take continued dedication from the people who made the Internet Invitational happen — and the golfers might want to cut down on the drinking, too.
